mainTopic: The creation of אדם and חוה (face or tail), modesty between men and women, and the יצר הרע and the organs
overview: This עמוד opens with the last words of the previous teaching: everything הקדוש ברוך הוא does is for the good. Next, רב הונא teaches in the name of רב and רבי מאיר that a person's words before ה׳ should be few. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא explains the double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר as two inclinations. The גמרא challenges that reading and offers two other explanations: 'woe to me from my Creator and from my inclination,' and the view that אדם הראשון was created with two faces. רב and שמואל then argue whether the צלע that חוה was built from was a whole face or only a tail. The גמרא tests each view against several פסוקים and answers every challenge. This leads into rules of modesty: a man should not walk behind a woman, along with the discussion of whether מנוח was an עם הארץ, and רבי יוחנן's ranked list of what not to walk behind, with exceptions for walking behind a בית הכנסת. The עמוד ends with teachings about the יצר הרע (a fly or wheat), the two advising kidneys, and a ברייתא listing the job of each organ, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Everything is for the good
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of the previous teaching (the story of רבי עקיבא): everything הקדוש ברוך הוא does is for the good.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does is] all for the good.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a teaching that started on the previous עמוד. Its message is that whatever הקדוש ברוך הוא does is for the good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words are the punchline of the story of רבי עקיבא, whose losses on a journey turned out to save him. Nothing new is argued here. The line simply seals the lesson before the גמרא moves on to a new teaching.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the end of a sentence that began on the previous עמוד (60b).

phrases.english: [He does] all for the good.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי עקיבא's saying from the end of 60b.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל לְטוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the teaching carried over from the previous עמוד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everything הקדוש ברוך הוא does is ultimately for the good.

steps.title: A person's words before God should be few
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, quoting רב in the name of רבי מאיר, teaches that a person should always keep his words few before הקדוש ברוך הוא. He brings a פסוק from קהלת as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב, quoting רבי מאיר: A person's words before the Holy One, Blessed be He, should always be few. The verse says: 'Do not be rash with your mouth, and do not let your heart rush to say something before God. For God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching: when you speak to ה׳, use few words. It supports this with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason comes from the פסוק itself. God is in heaven and you are on earth, and that huge gap calls for humility and careful speech. This fits the theme of this section of ברכות, which deals with proper conduct in תפילה and ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic standard for how a person should speak in תפילה: with care and restraint, not with rushed or excessive words.

steps.title: The double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר means two inclinations
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא explains that the double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר (creation of man) hints that ה׳ created two inclinations: the יצר טוב and the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught: Why is 'And ה׳ God formed (וַיִּיצֶר) man' written with two יו״דין? Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, created two inclinations, one good and one evil.
steps.whatsHappening: A new דרשה begins. The word וַיִּיצֶר is spelled with two יו״דין, and רב נחמן בר רב חסדא says this hints at two inclinations inside a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the word could be written with one יו״ד. The extra letter needs an explanation, and he reads the two יו״דין as two יצרים. The point is that man is uniquely created with an inner struggle between good and evil.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, created two inclinations,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: a דרשה on how man was created.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר hints that man was created with both a יצר טוב and a יצר הרע.

steps.title: Challenge: animals also have an inclination
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects. A בהמה's creation is not written with a double יו״ד, yet we see that animals damage, bite and kick, so they clearly have an inclination.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק strongly objected: If so, does an animal, about which וַיִּיצֶר (with two יו״דין) is not written, have no inclination? But we see that it damages, bites and kicks!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the previous דרשה. If two יו״דין mean two inclinations, then animals should have no inclination, and that is clearly false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is: if the double יו״ד is the source for having a יצר, then a creature without it should lack a יצר. But animals plainly have harmful urges. So the double יו״ד cannot be what teaches that a creature has inclinations.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then (introduces an absurd result)

phrases.notes: For animals the פסוק uses וַיִּצֶר with one יו״ד (בראשית 2:19).

phrases.english: does it have no inclination?
But we see

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the דרשה of רב נחמן בר רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the double יו״ד teaches that man has two inclinations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: by that reasoning animals, which lack the double יו״ד, would have no inclination. Observation shows that they do.

steps.title: New reading: woe from my Creator and woe from my inclination
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reinterprets the double יו״ד following רבי שמעון בן פזי. One יו״ד stands for יוצרי (my Creator) and one for יצרי (my inclination), and a person is caught between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, explain it like רבי שמעון בן פזי, who said: 'Woe to me from my Creator, and woe to me from my inclination.'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first reading, the גמרא offers a different explanation of the double יו״ד. It describes man's hard position between his Creator and his inclination.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two יו״דין now point to two forces pulling on a person, not to two internal inclinations. If he follows his יצר, he suffers from his Creator. If he follows his Creator, his יצר torments him. This reading survives the challenge, because animals face no such moral dilemma.
steps.whatToRemember: After the challenge, the double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר is explained by רבי שמעון בן פזי. Man is uniquely caught between his Creator and his יצר, and siding with either one brings 'woe' from the other. The next step offers a second explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: The final reading does not deny that man has a יצר הרע. It only rejects using the double יו״ד as the source for 'two inclinations.' The two letters now refer to Creator versus inclination.

phrases.english: Rather, [explain it] like Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
for Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said:
'Woe to me from my Creator,
and woe to me from my inclination.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּדְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected דרשה with a new reading that avoids the challenge about animals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The double יו״ד means man has two inclinations, good and evil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double יו״ד means man is caught between יוצרי (his Creator) and יצרי (his inclination). This dilemma is unique to man.

steps.title: Another explanation: אדם הראשון was created with two faces
steps.stepSummary: A second answer for the double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר. Following רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר, הקדוש ברוך הוא created אדם הראשון with two faces, male and female, as one body. The source is the פסוק 'אחור וקדם צרתני'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, the double יו״ד can be explained like רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר. He said that הקדוש ברוך הוא created two faces on אדם הראשון, as the פסוק says: 'Behind and before You formed me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain the two יו״דים in וַיִּיצֶר. They hint that אדם הראשון was formed with two faces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, the two יו״דים stood for two inclinations, and step 4 pushed back on that. Here the two יו״דים stand for two 'forms' (two faces) built into one person. The proof is the word צַרְתָּנִי, which comes from צוּרָה (form or face), together with 'behind and before', meaning a face in back and a face in front.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Behind and before You formed me' (תהלים קלט:ה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is a second answer to the same question: why does וַיִּיצֶר have two יו״דים?

steps.terutzMaskana: The two יו״דים refer to two faces (two forms) that אדם הראשון was created with.

steps.title: What was the צלע taken from אדם: a face or a tail?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'ויבן ה׳ אלהים את הצלע'. רב and שמואל disagree about what צלע means. One says a face (a whole side of אדם). The other says a tail (a small extra part, like a rib).
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And ה׳ God built the צלע.' רב and שמואל argue: one said it was a face, and one said it was a tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about how חוה was made and records a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about it. This is setting up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If צלע means 'face', this fits רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר: אדם had two faces, and one face was separated to become חוה. If צלע means 'tail', חוה was built from a small appendage, and אדם never had two faces.

keyTerms.meaning: Side or rib; here the part of Adam that חוה was built from
One said (we are not told which of the two)

phrases.english: 'And the Lord God built the tzela.'
phrases.notes: בראשית ב:כב

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree:
One said: it was a face.
And one said: it was a tail.
phrases.notes: A small appendage.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל: חַד אָמַר פַּרְצוּף. וְחַד אָמַר זָנָב.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of Adam's two faces by bringing a פסוק and a מחלוקת about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether the צלע was a whole face or only a tail.

steps.title: How does the 'tail' view explain 'behind and before'?
steps.stepSummary: The 'face' view fits the פסוק 'אחור וקדם צרתני' well. The גמרא asks how the 'tail' view, which holds that Adam did not have two faces, explains that same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'face': that is why it says 'Behind and before You formed me.' But for the one who says 'tail', what does 'Behind and before You formed me' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'tail' opinion. That view seems to have no explanation for the פסוק 'אחור וקדם צרתני'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בשלמא (granted) half shows that the 'face' view uses the פסוק as proof of two faces. The 'tail' view denies two faces, so the words 'behind and before' seem to have no meaning for it. The גמרא wants to know what that view does with the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (for one side)
According to the one who says
That is why it is written

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said 'face',
that is why it is written: 'Behind and before You formed me.'
But according to the one who said 'tail',
what is the meaning of 'Behind and before You formed me'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּרְצוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the 'tail' opinion from step 7 against the פסוק used in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the צלע was a tail
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אדם did not have two faces, the פסוק 'אחור וקדם צרתני' seems to have no meaning.

steps.title: רבי אמי: last in creation, first for punishment
steps.stepSummary: The 'tail' view reads the פסוק like רבי אמי. 'Behind' means man was created last, at the end of מעשה בראשית. 'Before' means man comes first for punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבי אמי, who said: 'Behind' refers to the work of creation, and 'before' refers to punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The 'tail' opinion does not read 'behind and before' as two faces. It reads the words as describing man's place in time and order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אחור and קדם are moved from a physical meaning (back face and front face) to an order meaning (last and first). Man was the last thing created, but he is first in line when punishment comes. Once the פסוק is read this way, it no longer proves two faces, so the 'tail' view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of creation (the six days)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'face' view reads 'אחור וקדם' as two physical faces. The 'tail' view reads it as order: last in creation, first for punishment.

phrases.english: It is like Rabbi Ami,
for Rabbi Ami said:
'Behind' refers to the act of creation,
phrases.notes: Man was created last.

phrases.english: 'and before' refers to punishment.
phrases.notes: Man is first for punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי אַמֵּי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8's challenge to the 'tail' view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אחור וקדם' must mean two physical faces, so the 'tail' view cannot explain it.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אחור וקדם' means last in creation and first for punishment, so it fits the 'tail' view.

steps.title: Which punishment does 'before' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that 'behind' means אדם was created last. It then asks which punishment 'before' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that 'behind' refers to creation, since man was not created until ערב שבת. But 'before' means first for punishment. Which punishment is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing רבי אמי's reading from Step 9. It asks for the specific punishment where man comes first, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'behind' half of the reading is easy to show from the order of creation. The 'before' half is only a general claim so far. The גמרא wants a specific event in the פסוקים where man is punished first.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (accepts one part before questioning another)

phrases.english: Granted, 'behind' refers to the act of creation
since he was not created until Shabbat eve
but 'and before' for punishment
the punishment of what?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא ״אָחוֹר״ לְמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the concrete case behind the 'before' half of רבי אמי's reading in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific punishment shows man being punished first?

steps.title: It cannot be the punishment after the snake
steps.stepSummary: Suppose 'before' meant the punishment after the נחש episode. A ברייתא of רבי says curses start with the least important. In fact the נחש was cursed first, then חוה, then אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say it means the punishment after the snake. But a ברייתא teaches that רבי says: with honor you start from the greatest, and with a curse you start from the smallest. With honor you start from the greatest, as it says that משה spoke to אהרן first and then to his sons אלעזר and איתמר. With a curse you start from the smallest: first the נחש was cursed, then חוה, and last אדם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious answer, the curses in גן עדן. It rejects that answer because אדם was cursed last there, not first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's rule says honor goes from greatest to smallest, and curses go from smallest to greatest. The rule is shown with a פסוק for each side: אהרן is named before his sons, and the curse order is נחש, then חוה, then אדם. So in the curses of גן עדן אדם was last, and that story cannot show man being 'first for punishment'.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches (introduces a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי's rule is not part of the answer. It is the reason the snake suggestion fails. The answer itself comes only in the next step.

steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'before for punishment' means the curses after the נחש episode.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's ברייתא shows that curses go from smallest to greatest, and אדם was cursed last. So that story does not put man first.

steps.title: It means the punishment of the flood
steps.stepSummary: 'Before' refers to the מבול. There the פסוק lists man first, 'מאדם ועד בהמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the punishment of the flood. The פסוק says: 'He wiped out every living thing on the face of the earth, from man to animal.' First man, then animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct answer to Step 10: the flood. In the flood man is named first for destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the מבול lists man before animals. This gives a clear case where man is 'first for punishment'. It completes רבי אמי's reading: man was last at creation and first at the flood.

keyTerms.meaning: The flood in the time of נח

steps.whatToRemember: According to the 'tail' view, 'אחור וקדם' means that man was created last (on ערב שבת) and was first to be punished in the מבול.

from man to animal'

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Before for punishment' meant the curses in גן עדן.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the מבול, where the פסוק names man before animals.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The punishment of the מבול, where the פסוק lists man before animals ('מֵאָדָם וְעַד בְּהֵמָה').

steps.title: How does the tail view explain the double יו״ד?
steps.stepSummary: The double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר fits the 'face' view, since two faces means two formations. According to the 'tail' view, what does the double יו״ד mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'face': that is why וַיִּיצֶר is written with two יו״דs. But for the one who says 'tail', what does וַיִּיצֶר teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns from the פסוק 'אחור וקדם' back to the double יו״ד. It challenges the 'tail' view, and this sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'face' view, the two יו״דs hint at two formed faces. The 'tail' view says there was only one face, so the two יו״דs seem to have no explanation. The גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
That is why it is written

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'face'
that is why 'vayyitzer' is written with two yods
but according to the one who says 'tail'
what is the meaning of 'vayyitzer'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּרְצוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the 'tail' view on 'אחור וקדם', the גמרא challenges it on a second point: the double יו״ד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double יו״ד suggests two formations, which fits two faces. The 'tail' view has no two faces, so it seems to leave the double יו״ד without a meaning.

steps.title: The double letter teaches two woes
steps.stepSummary: For the 'tail' view, the double יו״ד in וַיִּיצֶר does not mean two formations. It hints to רבי שמעון בן פזי's teaching that a person has two 'woes': one from his Creator and one from his inclination.
steps.simpleTranslation: It fits the teaching of רבי שמעון בן פזי, who said: 'Woe to me from my Creator, and woe to me from my inclination.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. According to the 'tail' view, the two יו״ד letters stand for two 'woes' that every person faces, not two faces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וַיִּיצֶר can be read as connected to יוֹצֵר (Creator) and to יֵצֶר (inclination). If a person follows his יצר הרע, his Creator punishes him. If he fights it, his יצר torments him. So the double letter shows that a person is caught between two pressures, and the 'tail' view no longer needs it to mean two formations.

keyTerms.meaning: My Creator (the One who formed me)
'And He formed', the word in the פסוק that is spelled with two יו״ד letters

steps.confusionAlert: יוֹצְרִי and יִצְרִי look almost the same, but they mean different things. The first means 'my Creator' and the second means 'my inclination' (my יֵצֶר). The whole teaching depends on that difference.

phrases.english: In line with Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
as Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said:
"Woe to me from my Creator,
phrases.notes: If I sin, my Creator punishes me.

phrases.english: woe to me from my inclination."
phrases.notes: If I resist sin, my inclination troubles me.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13 about the double יו״ד according to the 'tail' view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the extra letter as a moral teaching instead of a creation detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The double יו״ד proves there were two formations, which supports only the 'face' view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double יו״ד hints at the two 'woes' of יוצר and יצר, so the 'tail' view has no problem with it.

steps.title: How does the tail view explain 'male and female He created them'?
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'זכר ונקבה בראם' fits the 'face' view, since male and female were created together as one being. The גמרא asks what it means according to the 'tail' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says 'face'. That is why it is written 'Male and female He created them.' But for the one who says 'tail', what does 'Male and female He created them' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against the 'tail' view. A פסוק seems to say that male and female were created together from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חוה was a full face attached to אדם, then male and female really were created together at once. If she was only a tail, a small extra part, the פסוק's statement that both were created together seems too strong.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works well for one side (it sets up a contrast)
Face: the view that חוה was a full second face or side of אדם
Tail: the view that חוה was formed from a tail-like extension
'Male and female He created them' (בראשית ה:ב)

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'face',
that is why it is written "Male and female He created them";
but according to the one who says 'tail',
what is the meaning of "Male and female He created them"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּרְצוּף הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the double יו״ד is resolved, a new פסוק is brought to challenge the same 'tail' view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'tail' view of how חוה was created
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says male and female were created together. That fits a full second face, but not a mere tail.

steps.title: God first planned two but created one
steps.stepSummary: The 'tail' view explains 'זכר ונקבה בראם' through רבי אבהו. He pointed out a contradiction between two פסוקים and resolved it: God first planned to create two, but in the end created only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It fits the teaching of רבי אבהו, who pointed out a contradiction. It is written 'Male and female He created them', and it is also written 'For in the image of God He made man', which sounds like only one. How do they fit together? At first God thought to create two, and in the end only one was created.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge using רבי אבהו's resolution of two פסוקים that seem to clash. 'Male and female' describes God's original plan, not what was actually created.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק speaks of male and female, while another speaks of a single אדם. רבי אבהו explains that the first describes the plan and the second describes what actually happened. So the 'tail' view can say that only one being was created at first, and 'זכר ונקבה' refers only to the original thought.

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction (literally 'threw' two sources against each other)
In the image of God (בראשית ט:ו)
How can this be? (It introduces the resolution of a contradiction)
It arose in thought: the original plan

phrases.english: In line with Rabbi Abbahu,
for Rabbi Abbahu pointed out a contradiction:
It is written: "Male and female He created them,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב ״כִּי בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם״!
phrases.english: and it is written: "For in the image of God He made the man"!
phrases.notes: This sounds like only one being.

phrases.english: How can this be?
At first it arose in thought to create two,
and in the end only one was created.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ רָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק as describing the original plan rather than the actual creation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Male and female He created them' means two beings were actually created together.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to God's first thought. In practice only one was created, which fits the 'tail' view.

steps.title: How does the tail view explain 'He closed up the flesh'?
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'ויסגור בשר תחתנה' fits the 'face' view, because removing a whole side leaves a large opening that needs closing. The גמרא asks what it means according to the 'tail' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says 'face'. That is why it is written 'And He closed up the flesh in its place.' But for the one who says 'tail', what does 'And He closed up the flesh in its place' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another challenge against the 'tail' view, this time from the words describing how God closed up אדם after taking חוה from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a whole face or side was taken off אדם, a big open area would be left, so the פסוק needs to say that God closed it. If only a tail was removed, there seems to be nothing large that needs closing.

keyTerms.meaning: Side or rib: the part taken from אדם

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'face',
that is why it is written "And He closed up the flesh in its place";
phrases.notes: A whole side was removed, so there was an opening to close.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says 'tail',
what is the meaning of "And He closed up the flesh in its place"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּרְצוּף הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב ״וַיִּסְגֹּר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth challenge from the פסוקים against the 'tail' view, following the same pattern (after 'אחור וקדם', the double יו״ד, and 'זכר ונקבה').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Closing up flesh implies a large opening was left. That happens if a full side was removed, not just a small tail.

steps.title: Closing the place of the cut
steps.stepSummary: Several אמוראים, with the name of the speaker in doubt, answer that the closing of flesh was needed only for the spot where the tail was cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said, and some say רב זביד, and some say רב נחמן בר יצחק: It was needed only for the place of the cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even removing a tail leaves a wound at the spot where it was cut, and that small spot needed to be closed with flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that closing flesh requires a large opening. The answer shows that any cut needs closing, even a small one. So the פסוק fits the 'tail' view as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: it introduces a different version of who said the teaching
It was needed only for: it limits the פסוק to a narrow case

steps.whatToRemember: So far, each challenge against the 'tail' view has been answered: the double יו״ד means two woes, 'זכר ונקבה' was only the plan, and the closing of flesh was for the cut.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said,
and some say Rav Zevid,
and some say Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
It was needed only for the place of the cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the פסוק to a smaller case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Closing flesh means a large side was removed, which supports only the 'face' view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The closing was only for the small spot of the incision, which fits the 'tail' view too.

steps.title: How does the face view explain 'He built'?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns the challenge around. The word 'ויבן' fits the 'tail' view, since building a whole woman from a tail is real construction. It asks what 'building' means according to the 'face' view, where the face was already complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says 'tail'. That is why it is written 'And He built.' But for the one who says 'face', what does 'And He built' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches sides and challenges the 'face' view. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building means making something new. From a tail, God had to build a whole woman, so 'ויבן' fits well. If חוה was already a full face, there seems to be nothing left to build.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the switch. Until now every challenge was against the 'tail' view. Here the challenge is against the 'face' view.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says 'tail',
that is why it is written: "And He built";
phrases.notes: A whole woman had to be built from a tail.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says 'face',
what is the meaning of "And He built"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זָנָב הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the 'tail' view, the גמרא now challenges the opposite view, the 'face' view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'face' view of how חוה was created
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Building' implies making something new. A face that was already complete would not need to be built.

steps.title: Building means God braided חוה's hair
steps.stepSummary: The 'face' view explains 'ויבן' using רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. God 'built' חוה by braiding her hair before bringing her to אדם הראשון, because in the coastal cities braiding is called 'building'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explained like רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא taught: What does the פסוק 'And ה׳ built the צלע' mean? It teaches that the הקדוש ברוך הוא braided חוה's hair and then brought her to אדם הראשון. We know this because in the coastal cities they call braiding 'building'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19. According to the 'face' view, the word 'built' does not mean building a body. It means God braided חוה's hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that if חוה was already a complete face, there was nothing left to 'build'. The answer moves the meaning of 'ויבן' away from making her body and toward getting her ready, like a bride. A local usage of language (in the כרכי הים, braiding is called 'building') supports this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (the teaching of) Rabbi so-and-so
'Building', the local word for braiding hair

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 'face' view is saying God built חוה's body here. According to this answer, 'building' means hairdressing: getting her ready like a bride.

phrases.english: It is explained according to Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.
phrases.notes: This answers what ויבן means for the one who says it was a face.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya expounded:
What is meant by what is written: 'And ה׳ built the tzela'?

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁקִּלְּעָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחַוָּה,
phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, braided Eve's hair,
and brought her to Adam the first man —
for in the coastal cities
they call braiding 'building'.
phrases.notes: A proof from how people actually speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 on behalf of the 'face' view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the פסוק (ויבן = braiding)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ויבן' seemed to mean building a body, which fits only the 'tail' view.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ויבן' can mean braiding hair, so it fits the 'face' view too.

steps.title: Building means God shaped חוה like a storehouse
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation of 'ויבן', from רב חסדא or a ברייתא. God built חוה like a storehouse: narrow on top and wide on the bottom, so that she can carry a baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation of 'And He built': רב חסדא said, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: It teaches that the הקדוש ברוך הוא built חוה like a storehouse is built. A storehouse is narrow on top and wide on the bottom so that it can hold produce. So too, a woman is narrow on top and wide on the bottom so that she can hold a baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to explain 'ויבן' according to the 'face' view. Here 'built' means God shaped חוה's body in a special way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the face already existed, God still gave it a new body shape suited for carrying children. That shaping counts as 'building'. This is an alternative to the hair-braiding answer, not a rejection of it.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was said in another way)
A ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים)

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'And He built':
Rav Chisda said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: We're not sure who said this: either רב חסדא, an אמורא, or a ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבְּנָאָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחַוָּה
phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, built Eve
like the structure of a storehouse.
Just as this storehouse is narrow on top
and wide on the bottom
in order to hold the produce,
so too a woman is narrow on top
and wide on the bottom
in order to hold the baby.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״וַיִּבֶן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same question that Step 20 answered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With a ready-made face, there seems to be nothing left to 'build'.
steps.terutzMaskana: God built a body shape designed for carrying a baby, and that is the 'building'.

steps.title: God acted as the שושבין of אדם הראשון
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר learns from 'ויביאה אל האדם' that God served as שושבין for אדם הראשון. From here the תורה teaches that a great person should serve as שושבין for a lesser person and not feel bad about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He brought her to the man': רבי ירמיה בן אלעזר said: This teaches that the הקדוש ברוך הוא became the שושבין (best man) of אדם הראשון. From here the תורה taught proper conduct: a great person should go out of his way to be the שושבין for a lesser person, and it should not bother him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with the next words of the same פסוק and brings a new teaching. Because God Himself brought חוה to אדם, God acted as אדם's שושבין (best man).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leading the bride to the groom is the job of the שושבין. If God did this for אדם, then a great person should not feel it is beneath his honor to do the same for someone less important. This step is not part of the face/tail argument. It is a side teaching on the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Best man; the one who escorts and helps the groom
And it should not bother him (he should not feel it is beneath him)

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a lasting lesson in humility: honored people should gladly help others celebrate, even those of lower standing.

phrases.english: 'And He brought her to the man':
Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said:
It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, became
the best man of Adam the first man.
From here the Torah taught proper conduct:
that a great person should go out of his way to serve as best man for a lesser person,
and it should not bother him.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיְבִיאֶהָ אֶל הָאָדָם״, אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק and brings an independent teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God served as אדם's שושבין. Therefore a great person should serve as שושבין for a lesser person without feeling hurt in his honor.

steps.title: Which face walked in front?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a question on the 'face' view. If אדם was created with two faces, which face went in front when the being walked?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says it was a 'face': which of the two walked in front?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the 'face' view and asks a clarifying question about it. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first human was one body with a male face and a female face, it could walk in only one direction. So one face had to point forward. The גמרא wants to know whose face that was.

keyTerms.meaning: Face; the view that חוה was a second face of אדם

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against the 'face' view. It is a real question asking for more detail about how that view pictures the first human.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says 'face':
which one of them walked in front?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״פַּרְצוּף״, הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ סַגִּי בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the face/tail discussion and asks a detail question about the 'face' view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In the two-faced first human, which face led when it walked?

steps.title: The man's face walked in front
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that it is reasonable to assume the man's face led the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It makes sense that the man walked in front.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question: the male face was in front. The next step brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the word 'מסתברא', which means 'it is logical'. This shows the answer is based on reasoning, not on a direct פסוק. The reasoning comes from a known rule about walking behind a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical / it makes sense

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is reasonable that the man walked in front.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The male face was the front one.

steps.title: Proof: a man should not walk behind a woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן בר יצחק. A man should not walk behind a woman, even his own wife. On a bridge he should move her to the side. Someone who walks behind a woman crossing a river has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: A person should not walk behind a woman on the road, even his own wife. If he meets her on a bridge, he should move her to the side. And anyone who walks behind a woman in a river has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show why it makes sense that the man's face was in front. Proper conduct is for a man not to walk behind a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man walking behind a woman may keep staring at her. So it is fitting that God made the man's face the leading one. The ברייתא gets stricter step by step: the road, then the bridge (move her aside), then the river. In the river she lifts her clothing to cross, so following behind her carries the harshest punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
He should move her to the side
A share in the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: The 'face' view holds that אדם and חוה began as one two-faced being. The man's face led, because a man should not walk behind a woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא is also a practical rule of צניעות (modesty) that applies today, not just a proof about the creation story.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא יְהַלֵּךְ אָדָם אֲחוֹרֵי אִשָּׁה בַּדֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: As it was taught: A person should not walk behind a woman on the road,
even his own wife.
If she happens to meet him on a bridge —
he should move her to the side.
phrases.notes: So that he passes ahead of her instead of walking behind her.

phrases.english: And anyone who passes behind a woman in a river —
phrases.notes: She lifts her clothing to cross, so her skin is exposed.

phrases.english: has no share in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לֹא יְהַלֵּךְ אָדָם אֲחוֹרֵי אִשָּׁה בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's reasoning in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That the man's face walked in front in the two-faced first human.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding a man to walk behind a woman.

steps.title: Handing money to a woman in order to look at her
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a man who counts money from his hand into a woman's hand so he can look at her will not escape the judgment of גיהנם, even if he is as great as משה רבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If a man counts out coins from his hand into a woman's hand so that he can look at her, he will not be cleared from the judgment of גיהנם, even if he has as much תורה and as many good deeds as משה רבינו. As the פסוק says: 'Hand to hand, the evil one will not go unpunished.' This means he will not be cleared from the judgment of גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that continues the theme of the last step: behavior between men and women that is not modest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'hand to hand' in the פסוק as a man passing money from his hand into a woman's hand. The mention of משה רבינו hints that even someone who received the תורה hand to hand from ה׳ is not protected. The problem is not the money. It is using the handoff as an excuse to stare at her.

keyTerms.meaning: To look at or gaze at
He will not be cleared or go unpunished
גיהנם, the place of punishment after death

steps.confusionAlert: The issue is not handing money to a woman. The ברייתא is talking about someone who does it 'in order to look at her.' His intention is what makes it so bad.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who counts out coins to a woman
from his hand to her hand
in order to look at her,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בְּיָדוֹ תּוֹרָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים
phrases.english: even if he has Torah and good deeds in his hand
phrases.notes: In his hand means to his credit.

phrases.english: like Moshe our teacher,
he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehinnom.
As it says: 'Hand to hand, the evil one will not be cleared'
phrases.notes: משלי 11:21

phrases.english: meaning he will not be cleared from the judgment of Gehinnom.
phrases.notes: The 'evil' in the פסוק is understood as גיהנם.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּרְצֶה מָעוֹת לְאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the modesty theme of the ברייתא in step 25 with another case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who passes money hand to hand to a woman in order to look at her will not escape the judgment of גיהנם, no matter how great he is.

steps.title: רב נחמן says מנוח was an ignoramus
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that מנוח, the father of שמשון, was an עם הארץ, because the פסוק says he walked behind his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: מנוח was an עם הארץ, as it is written: 'And מנוח went after his wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן uses the rule from the earlier ברייתא, that a man should not walk behind a woman. He says מנוח broke it, which shows he was not learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads 'went after his wife' literally, meaning physically walking behind her. Since a learned person would know not to walk behind a woman, he concludes that מנוח was an עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: And he went after his wife

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Manoach was an ignoramus,
as it is written: 'And Manoach went after his wife.'
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:11

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מָנוֹחַ עַם הָאָרֶץ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule against walking behind a woman to a figure in תנ"ך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנוח was an עם הארץ because he literally walked behind his wife.

steps.title: The same wording is used about אלקנה and אלישע
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects: similar wording appears about אלקנה and about אלישע. Are we really going to say that these great people physically walked behind a woman?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objected: If so, what about אלקנה, where it is written, 'And אלקנה went after his wife'? And what about אלישע, where it is written, 'And he arose and went after her'? There too, did they literally walk behind her?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רב נחמן's literal reading. He points out that if we read the words that way, we would have to say the same thing about great צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלקנה was the father of שמואל הנביא, and אלישע was a נביא. Nobody would call them ignoramuses. So the phrase 'went after her' cannot automatically mean walking behind her physically.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (if we accept your logic)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak objected to this:
But if that is so,
regarding Elkanah, where it is written:
'And Elkanah went after his wife,'
and regarding Elisha, where it is written:
'And he arose and went after her,'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 4:30, about the שונמית woman

phrases.english: there too, did he literally go behind her?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the literal reading in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's literal reading of 'went after his wife'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same phrase is used about righteous people, so reading it literally would wrongly turn them into ignoramuses.

steps.title: Following her words and her advice
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'after her' means following her words and advice. The פסוק about מנוח means the same thing, so there is no proof that he was an עם הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means after her words and after her advice. Here too, by מנוח, it means after her words and after her advice.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק finishes his objection by offering a different reading. This knocks out רב נחמן's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Going after' someone can mean listening to them and doing what they say. Once that reading is clearly correct for אלישע, the same reading works for מנוח. So the פסוק no longer shows that he did anything wrong.

phrases.english: Rather, it means after her words and after her advice;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי אַחֲרֵי דְבָרֶיהָ וְאַחֲרֵי עֲצָתָהּ.
phrases.english: here too, it means after her words and after her advice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַחֲרֵי דְבָרֶיהָ וְאַחֲרֵי עֲצָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection of step 28 by giving the non-literal reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב נחמן's proof from the פסוק that מנוח was an עם הארץ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'went after' can mean following someone's advice, not walking behind them physically.

steps.title: רב אשי: by רב נחמן's view, מנוח never even learned in school
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that according to רב נחמן, מנוח did not even study חומש as a child. A simple פסוק shows that רבקה rode behind the man, not in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: According to what רב נחמן said, that מנוח was an עם הארץ, he did not even learn in school. As it says: 'And רבקה and her maidens arose, and they rode on the camels, and they went after the man.' After the man, and not in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי goes back to רב נחמן's opinion and shows how extreme it is. If מנוח really walked behind his wife, he was missing knowledge that schoolchildren have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a woman goes behind a man, and not the other way around, is already shown in a simple חומש story about רבקה. Children learn this in school. So, according to רב נחמן, מנוח's ignorance was very basic, not just a lack of deep learning.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to what he said
He did not read or learn (מקרא)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן reads 'walked after his wife' literally and calls מנוח an עם הארץ. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it as following her advice. רב אשי adds that by רב נחמן's view, מנוח did not even know the basic פסוק about רבקה riding behind אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And according to what Rav Nachman said,
that Manoach was an ignoramus,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בֵּי רַב נָמֵי לָא קְרָא,
phrases.english: he did not even study in children's school,
as it says: 'And Rivkah and her maidens arose,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:61

phrases.english: 'and they rode on the camels'
'and they went after the man'
and not in front of the man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וּלְמַאי דְּקָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב נחמן's view from step 27 and shows how far it goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב נחמן, מנוח lacked even the elementary knowledge, taught in the רבקה story, that a woman goes behind a man.

steps.title: Better to walk behind a lion than behind a woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a ranked list: walk behind a lion rather than a woman, behind a woman rather than עבודה זרה, and behind עבודה זרה rather than behind a בית הכנסת while the ציבור is davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Walk behind a lion and not behind a woman. Walk behind a woman and not behind עבודה זרה. Walk behind עבודה זרה and not behind a בית הכנסת while the people are davening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the topic of walking behind a woman. רבי יוחנן gives a ladder of three comparisons, each one worse than the one before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lion only puts the body in danger, but walking behind a woman can lead to bad thoughts, so it is worse. Walking behind עבודה זרה looks like you are honoring it, which is even worse. Worst of all is walking behind a בית הכנסת during davening, because you look like you are turning your back on the ציבור and on תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Idolatry, or an idol being carried in procession

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying a lion is safe or that idolatry is acceptable. It is a comparison of which is WORSE, and each step on the ladder is worse than the one before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Behind a lion and not behind a woman,
phrases.notes: Better to walk behind a lion. The danger to the body is less serious than the danger of bad thoughts.

phrases.aramaic: אֲחוֹרֵי אִשָּׁה וְלֹא אֲחוֹרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: behind a woman and not behind idolatry,
phrases.notes: Walking behind an idol looks like you are part of its procession.

phrases.aramaic: אֲחוֹרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְלֹא אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
phrases.english: behind idolatry and not behind a synagogue
at the time when the congregation is praying.
phrases.notes: He looks like he is cutting himself off from the ציבור's תפילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲחוֹרֵי אֲרִי וְלֹא אֲחוֹרֵי אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of walking behind a woman from the מנוח discussion and adds a ranked set of comparisons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ranked list of places to avoid walking behind: a woman is worse than a lion, עבודה זרה is worse than a woman, and a בית הכנסת during davening is worse than עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Four exceptions to walking behind a shul
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the rule about walking behind a בית הכנסת. It does not apply if the person is carrying something, if there is another entrance, if he is riding a donkey, or if he is wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he is not carrying anything. If he is carrying something, there is no problem. We only said this when there is no other entrance. If there is another entrance, there is no problem. We only said this when he is not riding a donkey. If he is riding a donkey, there is no problem. We only said this when he is not wearing תפילין. If he is wearing תפילין, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last part of רבי יוחנן's rule (the בית הכנסת) and narrows it with four exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is how it looks: people may think he is avoiding תפילה. In each exception, onlookers have an innocent explanation. He is busy carrying a load or riding, or he may be heading to another entrance, or his תפילין show that he is clearly connected to מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: And we only said this when... (a formula that limits a rule)
We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: The rule about walking behind a בית הכנסת is about how it looks to others. When there is an obvious innocent reason, the rule does not apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a model for how the גמרא handles appearance-based rules: the rule stops wherever the bad appearance stops.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא דָּרֵי מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: And we only said this when he is not carrying something,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי דָּרֵי מִידֵּי — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if he is carrying something, we have no problem with it.
phrases.notes: Everyone understands that he cannot go in while carrying a load.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: And we only said this when there is no other entrance,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if there is another entrance, we have no problem with it.
phrases.notes: People may assume he is walking to the other door.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא רְכִיב חֲמָרָא,
phrases.english: And we only said this when he is not riding a donkey,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל רְכִיב חֲמָרָא — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if he is riding a donkey, we have no problem with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא מַנַּח תְּפִילִּין,
phrases.english: And we only said this when he is not wearing tefillin,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַנַּח תְּפִילִּין — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if he is wearing tefillin, we have no problem with it.
phrases.notes: His תפילין show that he is not someone who throws off the yoke of מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא דָּרֵי מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the last clause of רבי יוחנן's rule with four exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walking behind a בית הכנסת during davening is allowed if he is carrying something, if there is another entrance, if he is riding a donkey, or if he is wearing תפילין.

steps.title: The evil inclination is like a fly
steps.stepSummary: רב says the יצר הרע is like a fly that sits between the two openings of the heart, and he brings a פסוק about flies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The יצר הרע is like a fly, and it sits between the two openings of the heart, as it says: "Dead flies make the perfumer's oil stink and bubble."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: what the יצר הרע is like. רב compares it to a fly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny fly can ruin a whole jar of fine perfume oil. In the same way, the יצר הרע is small but can spoil a person. רב places it at the heart, where a person's desires and decisions come from.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The evil inclination is like a fly
and it sits between the two openings of the heart,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״זְבוּבֵי מָוֶת יַבְאִישׁ יַבִּיעַ שֶׁמֶן רוֹקֵחַ״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "Dead flies make the perfumer's oil stink and bubble" (Kohelet 10:1).
phrases.notes: A small fly ruins something precious. The יצר הרע works the same way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: יֵצֶר הָרָע דּוֹמֶה לִזְבוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the walking rules to a new aggadic topic about the יצר הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע is like a fly and sits between the two openings of the heart.

steps.title: The evil inclination is like wheat
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and says the יצר הרע is like wheat, based on a wordplay between חטאת and חטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: It is like a kind of wheat, as it says: "Sin (חטאת) crouches at the door."
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different picture of the יצר הרע. He compares it to wheat instead of a fly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the word חטאת (sin) as hinting to חטה (wheat). The word "לפתח" (at the door) fits the idea that it waits at the openings of the heart.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin (read here as a hint to wheat)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
It is like a kind of wheat,
as it is said: "Sin crouches at the door" (Bereishit 4:7).
phrases.notes: Wordplay: חטאת (sin) sounds like חטה (wheat).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: כְּמִין חִטָּה הוּא דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion from רב's fly comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יצר הרע is like a kind of wheat, learned from the wordplay חטאת / חטה.

steps.title: Two kidneys: one advises good, one advises bad
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person has two kidneys. One gives him good advice and one gives him bad advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person has two kidneys. One advises him to do good, and one advises him to do bad.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the theme of good and bad forces inside a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תנ״ך the kidneys are described as a place of inner advice. The ברייתא splits them into one good counselor and one bad counselor. This sets up the next step, which asks which kidney is which.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A person has two kidneys,
one advises him for good
and one advises him for bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁתֵּי כְּלָיוֹת יֵשׁ בּוֹ בְּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the inner good and bad forces in a person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person has two kidneys: one advises good and one advises bad.

steps.title: The good kidney is on the right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that the good kidney is on the right and the bad one is on the left, and supports this with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it makes sense that the good one is on his right and the bad one is on his left, as it is written: "A wise man's heart is to his right, and a fool's heart is to his left."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a detail to the ברייתא, saying which kidney is which, and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not say which side each kidney is on. The גמרא says it is logical (מסתברא) that good is on the right, and proves it from the פסוק that links wisdom with the right and foolishness with the left. This פסוק comes right after רב's fly פסוק in קהלת.

keyTerms.meaning: And it makes sense, it stands to reason

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא pictures a person's inner life as two forces: the יצר הרע (a fly or wheat at the heart's openings), and two kidneys giving advice, with the good on the right and the bad on the left.

phrases.english: And it stands to reason that the good one is to his right
and the bad one is to his left,
as it is written: "A wise man's heart is to his right
and a fool's heart is to his left" (Kohelet 10:2).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּטוֹבָה לִימִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds which side each kidney is on and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the good-advising kidney is on the right and the bad-advising one is on the left.
steps.raayaSupportSource: קהלת 10:2: "לב חכם לימינו ולב כסיל לשמאלו"

steps.title: A ברייתא listing what each organ does
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the job of each organ: the kidneys advise, the heart understands, the tongue shapes words, the mouth completes them, the esophagus brings food in and out, and the trachea makes the voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The kidneys give advice. The heart understands. The tongue shapes the sounds. The mouth finishes shaping them. The esophagus takes in and lets out all kinds of food. The trachea produces the voice.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא was just talking about the kidneys giving advice, it brings a ברייתא that lists the job of each part of the body. This list continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 told us the kidneys give advice, and this ברייתא places that idea inside a bigger list of organs and their jobs. Notice that thinking is split up: the kidneys suggest what to do, while the heart is what understands. Speech is also split into steps, with the tongue shaping the sounds, the mouth finishing them, and the trachea supplying the voice itself.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Rabbis taught". This opening phrase introduces a ברייתא.
The kidneys advise, meaning they suggest what a person should do.
Cuts or shapes. It describes the tongue forming clear sounds.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the וֶשֶׁט and the קָנֶה. The וֶשֶׁט is the food pipe, and the קָנֶה is the windpipe, which makes the voice. These two terms come up again and again in ש״ס, especially in the laws of שחיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a side topic connected by association. The previous steps discussed the kidneys giving advice, so the גמרא now brings a ברייתא listing the roles of all the organs, starting with the kidneys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each organ has its own role: the kidneys advise, the heart understands, the tongue shapes speech, the mouth completes it, the esophagus handles food, and the trachea produces the voice.
